[2026-09-29 | AMZN | Overweight | +3.9% | +2.0% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Overweight, not the trader's outright Buy: the fundamental direction is settled but the entry is not, so open only 20–25 units of a 120-unit target near 246.67 (and nothing at all if the caller already holds more than ~40–45 units), with the second 20-unit tranche gated on a daily close back above 244.30 on above-average volume after a test of the 241.01–244.24 confluence. Cap total AMZN exposure at 45–50 units ahead of the unmodeled Q3 print, keep 238.50 as the tactical stop but size to a −5.55% gap toward ~233 rather than to that stop, and reserve the final ~50 units for a daily close above 252.64 on >40M shares (ideally above 256.09) or post-earnings confirmation of operating margin ≥13.7% with capex at or below Q2's $54.2B. A daily close below 239.80 cuts tactical adds back to ~40 units, below 235.50 reduce to 25, and any pre-earnings strength into 250.17–252.64 is a trim, not an add.

**Investment Thesis**: The bull wins direction; the bear and neutral win entry and sizing. That split is why this is Overweight rather than the trader's Buy, and it is also why Hold is wrong.

What no one rebutted, and what rules out Sell/Underweight: Q2 revenue of $200.6B grew +19.6% versus +16.6% in Q1, operating income rose +43.2% to $27.5B, operating margin expanded 226bp to 13.7%, H1 operating income grew +36.6% with margin at 13.4%, and marketing, G&A and stock-based comp all fell as a share of revenue — genuine operating leverage, not a one-off. Core H1 EPS of ~$3.63 versus ~$2.89 (+26%) survives stripping out the $62.8B non-cash equity mark, which the conservative correctly called a GAAP-distribution problem rather than a cash problem. TTM operating cash flow of $161.4B, $176.1B of cash and securities, ~0.91x gross debt/TTM OCF and ~$29.7B net cash ex-leases mean negative FCF (H1 −$27.0B, TTM −$11.6B on $98.4B H1 capex) is an investment-cycle story, not a solvency one. The aggressive analyst is right that waiting for positive FCF, flat debt and oversold RSI in an AI-capex cycle means buying after the repair.

The bear and neutral win the entry. AMZN at 246.67 sits below the 10-EMA (250.17), the 50-SMA (256.09) and the VWMA (251.34), with MACD's histogram re-widening to −0.657 after nearly crossing up on Sep 22 and RSI at 41.93 offering no oversold cushion; volume at 33.7M versus a ~33.9M average shows neither capitulation nor accumulation. That is a 1.06-ATR coil (ATR 5.60, bandwidth 6.65%, down ~78% in six weeks) perched 1.4% under the 250.2–252.6 shelf and only 2.3–3.2% above the 238.9–241.0 confluence — expansion is coming, but nothing in the evidence says higher, and the failed 259.50/259.49/259.00 rejections plus lower highs from 284.02 say the medium-term structure still leans lower. The aggressive analyst's claim that this R:R is paid for by the 242.50 confluence add fails on his own mechanics: a blind limit at 242.50 into a falling tape is averaging down into negative momentum, and by the time a daily close below 239.80 confirms, that tranche is already filled. Conservative and neutral were both right that the second tranche needs a reversal close, not just a price level.

Gap risk is the decisive correction to the trader's construction. The stop at 238.50 is 8.17 points (~1.46 ATR) below entry and structurally well placed below the 239.82 gap top and 238.93 retracement, but AMZN gapped −5.55% and +15.32% on 3–5x volume in this dataset: −5.55% from 246.67 is ~233.05, roughly 13.6 points of real risk. A stop that does not fill is not a risk cap, so the sizing must be built on the gap, not the stop. Equally, the conservative's "do not initiate at all" is over-corrected — with two-sided gaps, zero exposure forfeits the +15.32% path while the operating business compounds, and the prior AMZN record (07-22 to 07-30) shows heavy de-risking inside an intact rising 50/200 structure forfeited 12–22% of five-day alpha. The neutral's synthesis — smaller starter, confirmation-gated adds, pre-earnings cap at 45–50 units, post-confirmation path to 120 — is the calibration I adopt.

The prior decisions reinforce the front-end haircut rather than the direction. The 2026-09-22 Underweight at 254.98 worked (−3.3% raw, −2.1% alpha) and reached the 247 target; but its stated re-add condition — a daily close holding the 249.50–252 shelf, or a 256–257 retest — has not triggered, and price at 246.67 is below the 10-EMA. Meanwhile every mid-range AMZN starter in this book (09-09, 09-16, 09-17, 09-18) produced negative five-day alpha, and each reflection concluded that a lower-band tag must be a wait-for-confirmation event. That is exactly why Tranche 1 shrinks from 35 to 20–25 units and why the rating stops at Overweight: strong conviction to add at a mid-range print is not supported by the tape, while favorable fundamentals plus a definable 3.3%-away invalidation is.

What would change the call. Up to Buy on a daily close above 252.64 on >40M shares, ideally above 256.09 and with MACD above signal, or on Q3 evidence that operating margin holds at or above 13.7% with capex at or below Q2's $54.2B, TTM FCF improving, organic (ex-acquisition) revenue confirmed near high-teens and no markdown in the $122.3B equity book. Down to Hold/Underweight on a daily close below 239.80 that fails to reclaim within two to three sessions, a markdown of that book, debt past ~$150B while the current ratio deteriorates, or Q3 revenue growth materially below 19.6% with margin below 13.7%. First real test above is the three-times-rejected 259.50 shelf; my 258 target sits just below it.

Stated gaps, not filled: no earnings date, no valuation multiples or consensus EPS (so the only anchor remains ~31x core TTM and the aggressive's "already discounted" claim is unprovable), no 2027 capex guidance, no AWS segment revenue/margin/backlog (so capex ROI cannot be measured), no options-implied volatility or skew (so no overlay is priced), organic versus acquired revenue is not separable in the fundamentals extract, and the news sample is thin. No portfolio, holdings or cash context was provided, so all sizing is a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation and must be netted against any existing AI-capex exposure (NVDA, hyperscalers, other capex-heavy cloud names) — trimming AMZN while running those at full weight would be optics, not risk management. Any position carried through the Q3 print should be expressed with defined risk (a put spread) rather than a stop that a gap can skip.

**Price Target**: 258.0

**Time Horizon**: 3–6 months, re-scored at the Q3 print; the 1–3 week coil resolution (239.80 down / 252.64 up) takes precedence

REFLECTION:
Five days produced +3.9% raw and +2.0% alpha, so the Overweight direction was right, but a 5-day window cannot validate a 3–6 month thesis built on operating leverage and capex ROI — it only judges the coil. What it supports is the refusal to sit at zero exposure: the conservative "do not initiate" would have forfeited this move, and the coil resolved upward rather than into the 239.80 breakdown. What it undercuts is the confirmation-gating: the second tranche required a close above 244.30 and the final ~50 units a close above 252.64, so a 3.9% five-day advance likely ran past both triggers while only 20–25 units were on. Lesson for the next mid-range starter with a 3.3%-away invalidation and two-sided gap risk: keep the small starter, but pre-commit a partial add to plain strength (e.g., a close above the 10-EMA) rather than gating every tranche on the higher shelf.

[2026-09-28 | AMZN | Underweight | +2.1% | +0.9% | 5d]

**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is **Underweight**, not Sell: execute an immediate partial sale at market near 246.15 to bring a standard 5% single-name allocation down to roughly 2.5–3.0% (about half of standard weight), and place any residual reduction as limits into a bounce at 250.94–253.29 rather than queuing above spot. The tactical underweight is invalidated on a daily close above 253.29, with meaningful re-risk only on a second confirmation above 256.15 — and then in 25–50bp tranches. Ladder the residual on a closing basis: below 244.30 cut to ~1.5–2.0%, below 244.30 on volume above 45M cut to ~1%, below 240.94 (200-SMA) go to a full review of the remaining position. **Investment Thesis**: The bear/Research Manager case wins the current decision, but not by enough to justify a Sell, and the neutral seat's staged construction is the correct vehicle for it.

WHAT IS UNDISPUTED AND CAPS THE RATING AT UNDERWEIGHT RATHER THAN SELL: none of the three risk seats contested the operating franchise. Q2 revenue grew **+19.6%**, operating income **+43.2%** to **$27.5B**, operating margin **13.69%**, TTM operating cash flow **$161.4B**, cash and securities **$176.1B**, interest coverage **24.3x**. The long-term structure is technically intact: the 200-SMA at **240.94** is rising, the 50-SMA at **256.15** is above it, and the golden cross has not broken. The conservative analyst conceded the operating engine is not deteriorating; the aggressive analyst's own framing is a trim, not an exit. A full-exit Sell would be selling a business compounding operating income at 43% with $176B of liquidity while price sits 0.55% above support — that is not risk management, it is a momentum tantrum.

WHAT WINS THE DIRECTION: (1) The trend is a failed repair, not a base. AMZN closed **246.15**, below the **10-EMA 250.94**, **VWMA 251.72**, **20-SMA/Bollinger mid 253.29** and **50-SMA 256.15**; the 50-SMA slope collapsed from +3.81 points to +0.68 over ten sessions; the swing sequence is four lower highs (287.20 → 267.56 → 261.12 → 259.49 → 247.77). (2) Momentum: MACD **−2.35** below zero and below signal, with the histogram reset failing (compressing to −0.057 on 9/22 then widening back to −0.614 by 9/28) — a failed reset is a bearish tell, not a bottom. RSI at **41.24** is not oversold, so there is room to fall before capitulation. (3) The fundamental risk is capex/FCF/leverage, and no seat produced a repair: TTM FCF **−$11.6B**, H1 FCF **−$27.0B**, Q2 capex **$54.2B** or 27% of revenue (annualizing toward ~$217B against TTM OCF of $161.4B), long-term debt **+93.2%** to **$133.0B**, total debt **+80.5%** to **$146.4B**, interest expense **+155%** with coverage down from 35.5x to 24.3x, current ratio **1.03x**, **$78.1B** due inside twelve months, ROIC down from ~15% to **12.3%**, D&A **+31.3%** and capex/D&A at 2.30x.
